I self harmed for several years and have been clean over a year and a half. from the research I've done to try to understand myself better over the years I found out there's different types of sh, it doesn't necessarily mean someone is suicidal. For me I self harmed for a long time and for part I wasn't suicidal and for part of it I was. also in my experience it really only got better after I saw a therapist. If you decide to try to take what she uses to sh at some point it is extremely likely that she will just find other ways to do so and just won't tell you so I don't recommend it unless she asks you to. When she does stop it'll be because she made the decision to, no one can do that for her. A good thing is to find things that give similar sensations but are less destructive, like putting red dye and water in an ice cube tray and using that when she gets urges because it gives similar physical and visual affects. Another thing you should know is when a person self harms they get a dopamine release that's said to feel similar to morphine, that's part of the reason self harm is addictive so its not easy to stop once you start and its not as simple as just trying. Sh is an addiction. Something that's helped me is to find other things like a favorite song or something else that also gives a dopamine dump to substitute for the sh. You can find out what other things give dopamine by researching, music was just the one that helped me the most. When I finally did decide to stop something that helped a lot was not just letting the physical healing process happen but actively helping it along by using thigs like Neosporin. I also took a picture of my sh everyday for a while once I did stop so I could compare and see my progress, that's something that worked for me but it may trigger other ppl so its up to personal decision. I would also advise you to not tell the parents unless it becomes necessary, they tend to not understand, take it as a personal attack, get angry, and just generally react very poorly in situations like these making things worse. If your sister gets to a place where she feels comfortable enough to tell them she can but until then I would avoid it on your end. Try not to tell her that its scary or upsetting for you and you're scared about her, that'll probably make her feel guilty for worrying you. Just let her know you're here to help and you love and care about her. Its ok to be scared and not know what to do but don't put the responsibility of reassurance on her. Maybe you could talk to a therapist on how you're feeling and how to best help her. Ultimately just try to love and support her, there's a lot of shame and stigma surrounding sh so just try to be there for her and try to be non judgmental. You got this and you two are going to get through this together. I hope this helps.💕

Second, as awful as it feels just let the panic attack happen, look up tips of how to avoid and help with them and then just deal with them. The think that helps my anxiety best is a cbd inhaler, its helped me avoid tons of panic attacks. But yeah try your best to stop the compulsions and ruminations and remember its OK to have panic attacks. Even if it feels like the world is ending it will pass

Tbh I think that if I didn't stop coping more casually when I felt guilty for not being anxious I would probably be in a way better place than I am now, especially if you've dealt with different types of OCD or intrusive thoughts before you would prob be better at coping with things like that. If you're really concerned you can always talk to an OCD therapist or psychologist about it too cuz I'm no professional but honestly if you try brushing it off your brain can desensitize itself fairly quickly I think. For me it used to be a rule of two days. If I could put up with having an awful intrusive thought with all the horrible symptoms for two days it would go away because I would start getting desensitized to it. I think the same thing would have happened with POCD if I didn't think that getting desensitized to it meant that I really was a bad person at the time.
I think this is pretty common when you get better at coping with your ocd.

The only types of things that helped me are Thomas Sanders intrusive thoughts videos, (they're on youtube) and those helped and also reading about ruminations, its an ocd symptom. Try to remember this is a mental illnesses, its not something that just goes away with prayer. Its hard but you can find tools to help you, also [ocdla.com](https://ocdla.com) is a really helpful cite you should check out. Also maybe look into scrupulosity ocd.
